intro: The 3.11 features engineering projects use most are asyncio.TaskGroup, except* and tomllib. This section combines them in one polling scenario: read a device list from TOML, poll concurrently, and handle failures by exception type.
example_desc: M01 is healthy, M02 times out and M03 refuses the connection at once. Note the output: as soon as M03 fails, TaskGroup cancels the other tasks, so M01 returns nothing even though it needs only 0.01 s, and M02 never reaches its timeout. That is TaskGroup's one-fails-all-cancel semantics.

case.title: One device goes offline and the whole batch loses its data
paragraphs: A project replaced asyncio.gather with TaskGroup and found that one device refusing a connection wiped out the readings of every other device in the batch. This is by design: TaskGroup suits work that only makes sense when every part succeeds, such as the steps of one transaction.

Device polling usually wants independent results. Catch expected exceptions inside read() and return a reading with bad quality, so TaskGroup only sees real programming errors; or give each device its own TaskGroup.
steps: Decide whether a batch is all-or-nothing or independent.
For independent work, handle expected exceptions (timeouts, refused connections) inside the coroutine.
Use except* to handle every exception in an ExceptionGroup, not just the first.
Read configuration with tomllib; no third-party toml package is needed.

updates.text: Python 3.11 has received security fixes only since 2026 and is expected to reach end of life in October 2027. New projects should use 3.13 or later.

exercises.q: What is the simplest change that keeps M01's result?
exercises.a: Catch ConnectionError and TimeoutError inside read() and return something like (name, None) instead of raising. TaskGroup then has no reason to cancel the other tasks.

exercises.q: If M03's delay becomes 0.03 (no refusal), what is printed?
exercises.a: M01 and M03 succeed and M02 times out at 0.05 s. When TaskGroup receives the TimeoutError the other two have already finished, so their results are kept: "1 device(s) timed out" plus two successful readings.

exercises.q: How does except* TimeoutError differ from except TimeoutError?
exercises.a: except* matches exceptions inside an ExceptionGroup and several except* clauses can run for one group. A plain except matches a single exception and does not catch the ExceptionGroup raised by TaskGroup.
No, it only reads. Use a third-party package such as tomli-w to write.
